_comment: The teacher-facing lesson builder, from the goal-index modal. The whole running order of the lesson is ONE section, `plan`, and ONLY the subject families write it: it is null here and listed in `familyOnly`, so a tree without a `subjectFamily` (and without its own `lessonPlan.plan` prompt row) gets a validation error instead of a lesson plan with no plan in it. In a lesson plan the plan IS the subject's didactics, which is why there is no general default. A teacher who wants a different lesson rewrites that one section and nothing else has to follow (from 4.0.0; before that the starter, the rounds, the diagnostic question and the retrieval were five sections that referred to each other). No other section names a part of the lesson, for the same reason. The engine computes no timetable (from 3.0.0). `groups` is the order of the sections AND the headings they are shown under, both in the builder and on /prompts/ and in the instruction a student pastes ("## Role and style"); each group's `description` says what is in it, for the builder. `when` names the condition a section has, from CONDITIONS in engine.js; a section without one always renders. A section that is null here is filled by another layer: outputLanguage and writingStyle by the language file, nodeInstruction and aids by the engine, `plan` by the subject family, and `extra` by the teacher, in a prompt row in tree.csv. `movedTo` names, for each section that existed before 4.0.0 and does not now, the section its text went into; /prompts/ uses it when comparing two releases, so a merged section reads as moved and not as deleted. The engine ignores it.
title: Lesson plan generator

groups.title: Role and style
groups.description: Who the AI is, how the answer is laid out, and the language it is written in.

groups.title: The lesson
groups.description: The learning goals and the plan for the whole lesson, part by part: starter, teaching each goal, diagnostic questions and retrieval. Plus how concept and fact goals are taught.

groups.title: Context
groups.description: What the students already know, the aids they may use, and anything particular to the course.

groups.title: Extra
groups.description: Your own additions. Empty unless you write something here.

sections.role: You are an experienced subject-teaching specialist helping a teacher, not a student, plan one lesson in {courseName}. Reply with the lesson plan straight away: no clarifying questions and no summary of these instructions. The teacher can ask for changes afterwards.
sections.format: Write the answer as one continuous document the teacher can read from top to bottom while teaching, with a heading and a minute marking for each part, in the order of the lesson. Put everything shown to students in its own block that starts with "On the board:" on a line of its own, written exactly as it should appear and with no teacher instructions inside. Put everything else, such as what the teacher does and says, the answers and what to look for, outside these blocks. Give complete answers to all problems in paragraphs marked "Answers", outside the board blocks. Keep the text for students free of pedagogical jargon.
sections.goals:
The lesson should cover the following learning goals, in this order:
{goalList}
sections.conceptAdaptation: Goals marked [concept] are declarative knowledge, not skills. Teach them with examples and non-examples of the concept; the students' own work is deciding whether new cases are examples and why, or explaining the concept in their own words, and practice on them is qualitative. Keep the procedure minimal: practising it belongs to a separate goal further down the tree.
sections.factAdaptation: Goals marked [fact] are lists to know by heart: one item per "cue: answer", or a rule that generates the items. Teach these without worked examples: the teacher presents the list briefly, and the students' own work is short retrieval practice (cover the answers and recall them, both ways where that makes sense, in pairs or on mini-whiteboards). Bring the list back once more before the lesson ends.
sections.prerequisites:
The students already know the following, which today's goals build on. Use these words freely and draw on them throughout the lesson.
{prerequisiteList}
sections.prerequisitesNone: No prerequisites are recorded for today's goals: assume the topic is new to the students.
sections.aids:
Keep to the correct aids in the problems you write, by each learning goal's level (shown in the list above):
{aidsText}
